Chapter 134: 0131 Even Well-Known Authors Can Be Old-School Netizens

Of the dozens of contestants waiting for an autograph, more than half hadn't brought a copy of *Those Happenings in the Ming Dynasty*.

Someone even took out their semi-final invitation, asking Chen Guiliang to sign it directly.

"Hold on, buddy, couldn't you at least find a small notebook?" Chen Guiliang said with a laugh.

The other contestants burst into laughter.

That contestant didn't feel awkward at all. On the contrary, he argued confidently, "If you sign it, I can keep it together with the invitation."

Someone else asked, "Chen Guiliang, is Peking University fun? I'm planning to apply there too."

Chen Guiliang bluffed, "The Yuanpei Program is especially fun. You can pick any course in the entire university. You can study whatever you want. If you can get into Peking University, you should apply for the Yuanpei Program."

"Really?" The unlucky kid was intrigued.

Signing autographs and chatting idly, they finally finished after quite a while.

"Hi, senior."

A young girl who was helping out at the sign-in table waved.

Chen Guiliang had a vague impression of her. "You are?"

The young girl said, "My name is Zhang Yiwei. I won the first prize in Group B last year, and this year I'm competing in Group A. When you had your book signing in Shanghai a few days ago, I even went to show my support."

"Thank you very much," Chen Guiliang said.

The girl took out another book. "This is a sample copy of my essay collection, it'll be officially published next month. I'm not just giving it to you, I've already given out several copies today."

Chen Guiliang was slightly surprised and joked, "Not even giving us a chance to buy the book?"

The girl said, "The first print run isn't very large, so many bookstores won't have it."

Chen Guiliang flipped through the essay collection for a few pages and found the style was similar to Guo Xiaosi's. He casually said, "I'll recommend it on my blog for you."

"That would be great," the girl said, very happy.

This young girl was currently a high school senior. She would enter Fudan University's philosophy department this year and later become a professor at Fudan.

"Chen Guiliang!"

A voice called out. Chen Guiliang turned his head to see Cao Wenxuan, the deputy director of the Chinese department at Peking University, calling him.

Besides Cao Wenxuan, there were professors from other prestigious universities as well.

They were all judges.

The admissions officers from various universities would also come this year. But getting a reduced score requirement would be difficult. They would just put the first-prize winners on a "high-priority admissions watchlist," and they could be admitted as long as they met the minimum enrollment score.

There were also those who had applied for independent admissions in advance. As long as they passed the written test and had the New Concept award as a bonus, they could basically pass the interview.

Chen Guiliang ran over to join them.

Professor Chen, the director of Fudan's Chinese department, jokingly chided him, "You're a real piece of work, kid. You actually stood me up last year and quietly went to Peking University."

"I didn't stand you up," Chen Guiliang protested. "Before I applied to Peking University, I specifically called Director Chen and Director Wang."

Professor Xu from Nankai University said, "That Xiaonei.com of yours didn't reach our school until almost the end of the semester. During the final exams, I heard a group of students chatting excitedly outside the examination hall. I thought they were discussing the final exam questions. But when I got closer, I heard they were actually discussing which girl to vote for as the campus belle!"

"Hahahaha!" The professors roared with laughter upon hearing this.

Professor Lin from Xiamen University said, "Our school hasn't had a campus belle election yet."

"Professor Lin was the campus belle back in the day," said Professor Cheng from Sun Yat-sen University.

Amidst the laughter, Professor Lin said in a serious tone, "Don't you laugh. If there had been voting back then, I really might have been elected campus belle. I was very fashionable and beautiful when I was young. Not anymore, I'm almost fifty now."

Chen Guiliang said, "After the new year, I'll expand Xiaonei.com to Xiamen University as soon as possible. When we hold the campus belle election for Xiamen University, we'll open a special channel just for Professor Lin."

Professor Tong from Beijing Normal University said, "You can't go back on your word now. You have to do what you say."

Professor Lin waved her hands repeatedly. "Don't drag me into this."

A group of professors was waiting for the elevator there. When the other contestants saw Chen Guiliang chatting and laughing with the professors, they all cast envious glances his way.

The parents were even more envious, wishing Chen Guiliang was their son!

It wasn't dinnertime yet, so Chen Guiliang followed the group to a small lounge upstairs for tea and conversation.

Before long, the author judges arrived, the lineup more or less the same as last year.

The moment Yu Hua saw Chen Guiliang, he said, "Damn it, my royalty is only 12 percent, and you got 15 for your first book."

Chen Guiliang corrected him, "It's a tiered royalty with a 15 percent guarantee. Based on the current sales figures, I should end up getting 20."

"Is that something a human should say?" Yu Hua pointed at Chen Guiliang and turned to the other authors.

Su Tong said, "This kind of person deserves a beating. So infuriating!"

Ye Zhaoyan asked curiously, "With such a high royalty for the author, can the publisher still make a profit?"

Before Chen Guiliang could answer, Ma Yuan said with a smile, "Would anyone do business at a loss?"

Yu Hua said, "Next time I publish a book, I'll look for Chen Guiliang's publishing company too."

Of course, he was just saying that. They wouldn't easily switch publishers.

Cheng Cun said, "That San Guo Sha of yours is pretty good. I even bought a membership and I've been playing it every day this month."

"You actually play it?" Chen Guiliang was surprised.

Last year, he had asked some of the authors for their contact information. Some were willing to give it, while others just brushed him off.

For those who left their phone numbers, Chen Guiliang had sent text messages inviting them to play San Guo Sha.

After all, this man was 50 years old, his hair already turning gray!

Cheng Cun said, "Why can't I play? Let me tell you, besides being the artistic director of Rongshu Xia, last year I also became the chief moderator of 99read.com, and I'm also the moderator of 'Xiaozhong Caiyuan'."

Chen Guiliang said, "Understood, you're an old-school netizen."

Cheng Cun said smugly, "Not only do I play San Guo Sha myself, I also dragged Ah Cheng into it."

"The Ah Cheng who wrote *The Chess Master*?" Chen Guiliang asked.

"Who else could it be?" Cheng Cun said.

Chen Guiliang couldn't help but chuckle.

San Guo Sha was also a type of card game, so it was understandable for Ah Cheng, who wrote *The Chess Master*, to play it.

Cheng Cun even complained, "Ah Cheng is too stingy. He earns so much in royalties, but he's not willing to spend money when he plays games."

Well, so he was a free-to-play player.

Yu Hua asked, "Is San Guo Sha that interesting? Chen Guiliang sent me a text, but I couldn't be bothered to download it at the time."

Cheng Cun strongly recommended it, "It's really fun, I'm not kidding. I haven't even been writing lately. I spend all day on the forums, and when I'm tired of posting, I play San Guo Sha."

"Then I'll download it when I get back too." Yu Hua was also about to get hooked.

Chen Guiliang planned to send them physical card decks another day. Perhaps Yu Hua would even drag Shi Tiesheng along to play a few rounds.

Tie Yi wasn't interested in this. She asked, "Chen Guiliang, are you joining the Writers Association?"

The Writers Association here specifically referred to the China Writers Association, of which Tie Yi was currently the vice-chairwoman.

Chen Guiliang asked, "Am I qualified?"

"You are," Tie Yi said.

"Then I'll join." Chen Guiliang was indifferent about it.

Tie Yi said, "When it's time to recruit new members during the election, I'll have someone call and inform you."

Chen Guiliang thanked her.

Cao Wenxuan said, "You might as well join the Beijing Writers Association too."

Cao Wenxuan was the vice-chairman of the Beijing Writers Association.

"Alright, I'll join them all." Chen Guiliang accepted all offers.

Anyway, he just had to keep his distance from certain authors in the future. As for the association's activities, he would have to see if he had time to participate.

This year, these professors and authors were all quite enthusiastic towards Chen Guiliang.

It was definitely not just because of *Those Happenings in the Ming Dynasty*. The fact that Chen Guiliang had opened two companies was also one of the reasons.

Of course, the sales momentum of *Those Happenings in the Ming Dynasty* and the royalty percentage Chen Guiliang received were indeed shocking enough to the literary world.

They had been writing for so many years and had never seen anyone get a 20 percent royalty!

That night, Chen Guiliang was dragged out for drinks by Yu Hua and Cheng Cun, and he returned to his hotel room drunk to sleep for the night.

The next day's activities had nothing to do with him; he only needed to attend the final award ceremony. The media would be there then, so Chen Guiliang was just making an appearance to support the event.

While the contestants went to compete, Chen Guiliang headed straight for Dragon TV.

The show he was going to record was *Oriental Night Talk*, China's earliest talk show. This thing was about to break viewership records this year.

Usually, they invited celebrities as guests. Chen Guiliang wasn't actually qualified enough.

But it was almost the New Year, and there were no film or television works that needed promoting. The celebrities were busy with gigs or going home for the holiday.
